sources.entry: Deleterr - Automated media cleanup tool that removes watched and stale content from Plex, Sonarr, and Radarr based on configurable rules. MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: Deleterr is a YAML-configured tool that uses Radarr, Sonarr, and Tautulli to find and delete Plex media based on watch history, age, and exclusion rules.
summary.what_it_does: Deleterr identifies and deletes media files from a Plex library using criteria such as watch history, content age, and streaming availability. It works through Radarr, Sonarr, and Tautulli, and supports multiple Radarr/Sonarr instances, including separate regular and 4K libraries. Exclusions can be set by genre, actor, collection, JustWatch streaming availability, and Trakt lists. A dry run mode, on by default, logs what would be deleted without removing anything. A "Leaving Soon" feature tags candidates in a Plex collection or label, notifies users by email, Discord, Slack, or Telegram, and deletes them on the next scheduled run. A built-in scheduler supports daily, weekly, or custom cron schedules, and a one-time run mode is available.
use_cases: Delete unwatched movies and shows from Plex automatically
Free up disk space by removing stale media
Preview cleanup rules with a dry run before deleting
Warn Plex users before content is removed
Protect titles via Trakt lists or streaming availability
Manage separate 4K and regular Radarr/Sonarr libraries
how_to_run: Create config/settings.yaml from the provided settings.example.yaml and adjust settings
Add the ghcr.io/rfsbraz/deleterr:latest image to a docker-compose file with a ./config:/config volume
Or run once: docker run -v ./config:/config ghcr.io/rfsbraz/deleterr:latest --run-once
stack: Python-independent container image published to GHCR and Docker Hub
notable: Entire configuration in one YAML file that can be versioned in Git
dry_run is enabled by default so nothing is deleted until turned off
Leaving Soon grace period with Plex collections and notifications
Exclusions from Trakt lists, MDBList lists, and JustWatch availability
README includes a comparison with Maintainerr describing when to pick each
caveats: Works only with Plex; the README says Jellyfin and Emby are not supported
Requires Radarr, Sonarr, and Tautulli to be set up
The README warns not to use it with media you cannot afford to lose
Recycle bin recovery is not recommended for remote mounts
